name: Nirlon Ltd
title: Nirlon Ltd - 500307 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Fully leased NKP park (99.7% occupancy) with contracted escalations; FY26 PAT +59% flattered by Rs 69.5 cr deferred-tax write-back, ex-item growth ~27%; management evasive on cash of ~Rs 278-287 cr parked in FDs and on the 5% debt amortisation.

summary.headline: Nirlon Q4 FY26 PAT rose 32% YoY to Rs 71 crore; FY26 PAT Rs 346 crore includes Rs 69.5 crore one-time deferred tax gain; final dividend Rs 15/share.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was about Rs 174 crore (+9% YoY), EBITDA about Rs 136 crore (+8%) at a stated 77.85% margin, and PAT about Rs 71 crore (+32%). For FY26, total income was about Rs 683 crore (+6%), EBITDA Rs 535 crore (+5%), and PAT Rs 346 crore (+59%), with PAT growth of about 27% excluding a one-time Rs 69.5 crore deferred tax re-measurement gain after the move to Section 115BAA. Average occupancy across NKP and Nirlon House was 99.7% in Q4, with about 8,000 sq ft vacant at 31 March 2026. The Board proposed a final dividend of Rs 15/share (total FY26 dividend Rs 30 versus Rs 26 previously), and management stressed consistency over a large payout. Much of the Q&A was evasive on cash deployment, Nirlon House, REIT or structure plans, buybacks and valuation.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 346 crore; PAT margin 50.64%; includes one-time Rs 69.5 crore deferred tax re-measurement adjustment
financial_highlights.change: +59% YoY; about +27% excluding the one-time item

financial_highlights.metric: Average occupancy (NKP + Nirlon House), Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.change: Total FY26 Rs 30 vs Rs 26 in FY25 (per management)

financial_highlights.value: About Rs 278-287 crore (figure cited differently by analysts and management); maturity 6 months to 1 year; yield about 5.5%

segments.name: NKP (Nirlon Knowledge Park)
segments.commentary: Leasing rate was cited by an analyst as north of Rs 185/sq ft/month at 80% efficiency in Feb 2026; management said few renewals fall due in FY27 and no new renewal pricing was disclosed. Average occupancy is part of the combined 99.7%.

segments.name: Nirlon House
segments.commentary: No significant update on sale; management said it has 12-13 owners, so transactions take considerable time.

guidance_outlook: No specific guidance given on revenue, margins or PAT.
Dividend policy: management intends consistent, progressively higher payouts; new tax regime expected to enable significantly higher dividends in future, though not guaranteed.
Management declined to speculate on a special dividend or on use of the surplus cash.

HSBC loan amortisation: 5% per year from May 2027 for five years, then a bullet payment for the remaining balance (about 75% per the analyst's reading, flagged for confirmation). Outstanding loan cited at about Rs 1,150 crore by an analyst.
capex_capacity: Capex is focused on maintaining the park as an A-grade asset, including sustainability-related modifications; management said there is nothing significant planned outside the park.
No data centre or FSI expansion plans to comment on at this time.
Asked about the 31 March 2026 valuation, management cited about Rs 6,650 (FY26) versus about Rs 6,500 (FY25) without stating the cap rate; it declined to explain assumptions on the call.
demand_pricing: Average occupancy 99.7% in Q4 FY26; about 8,000 sq ft vacant at 31 March 2026.
Management said there are no significant early exits and no major renewals in FY27; NKP licensee renewals are being pursued through operational improvements.
Management noted growth comes from escalating contracted licence fees, new licences and some transactions at higher prices.
Management welcomed GCC expansion in India as positive for employment but did not link it to Nirlon's leasing.

qa_highlights.question: Why distribute only Rs 15 final dividend when cash is about Rs 300 crore, and what is the plan for the remaining cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited consistency and sustainability of dividends, moving from Rs 26 to Rs 30 for the year, and the new tax regime as enabling higher future payouts. It would not commit to a special dividend or a specific use for the surplus cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will surplus FD cash (about Rs 278 crore) be used to repay the HSBC loan (about Rs 1,150 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: No concrete plan yet; the company will follow the existing HSBC agreement. Next repayment is 5% in May 2027. FD yield is about 5.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will lease renewals in the next year be at higher rates, and have renewal talks started?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early for specific discussions on 2026-27 and 2027-28 renewals, with focus on licensee experience.

qa_highlights.question: Can NAV rise by a similar 15-20% as peer REITs after the 31 March 2026 valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would revert on the valuation; later it cited about Rs 6,650 vs about Rs 6,500 previously, but declined to explain the cap rate on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Why adopt the new tax regime now, and does this shelve a REIT restructuring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it moved to the new regime to optimise existing efficiencies and did not rule out future structures or transactions, without confirming any plan.

qa_highlights.question: Is buyback an option to return cash, and why was the FD placed at 5.5% while the HSBC loan costs about 7.75%?
qa_highlights.answer: Buyback is not under consideration at this point, for various reasons. On the FD versus loan spread, management said nothing concrete on the deployment of cash had been decided.

risks_watch: Idle cash of about Rs 165-300 crore (post-dividend) and negative carry versus the HSBC loan at about 7.75%; capital allocation remains undecided.
Lease renewal pricing and tenant retention: the next major renewal cohort (about Rs 3.26 lakh/sq ft per an analyst's reading of the presentation) is due in 2027 and terms were not discussed.
Margin pressure: an analyst noted total expenses up about 11% against income up about 5.9%, with EBITDA margin down from 79.33% to 78.36%; management promised an explanation later.
Tax efficiency for minority shareholders: dividends are taxed at shareholder level, and management did not address buyback or REIT alternatives.
Reconciliation of the lease expiry schedule (about 3,000 sq ft expiring in 12 months) versus 40% of other financial liabilities classified as current; management will respond offline.
Shareholding and promoter classification questions (Brookfield above 10%) were not answered.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on operations and the tax-driven PAT growth but evasive on capital allocation, Nirlon House, valuation assumptions, promoter reclassification, buybacks and structure plans, repeatedly deferring to written follow-up through Valorem Advisors.

growth.why: No numeric revenue or margin guidance; management says growth comes from escalating contracted licence fees, new licences and higher-priced transactions, with 99.7% occupancy and no capacity additions outside the existing park.
